citation: Koo TK, Li MY. A guideline of selecting and reporting intraclass correlation coefficients for reliability research. J Chiropr Med 2016;15(2):155-163
status: published; no correction found (not exhaustively checked)
results_effects_uncertainty: Describes 10 ICC forms; requires reporting software, model, type, definition; labels <0.5 poor, 0.5-0.75 moderate, 0.75-0.9 good, >0.9 excellent applied to the 95% CI (cut-points SECONDARY)
limitations_coi: Cut-points are conventions, not evidence of adequacy for any decision
tentsr_applicability: Defines ICC choice for Stage 2: two-way, absolute agreement, single measurement

citation: Weir JP. Quantifying test-retest reliability using the intraclass correlation coefficient and the SEM. J Strength Cond Res 2005;19(1):231-240
results_effects_uncertainty: ICC = relative consistency, SEM = absolute consistency; SEM and MDC (1.96*sqrt2*SEM) formulas (formulas SECONDARY via citing papers)
limitations_coi: Formulas confirmed only via citing literature
tentsr_applicability: Stage 2 SEM/MDC computation

citation: Hopkins WG. Measures of reliability in sports medicine and science. Sports Med 2000;30(1):1-15
results_effects_uncertainty: Within-subject variation (typical error), change in mean and retest correlation as main reliability measures; typical error as CV% when error scales with magnitude
limitations_coi: Advocates magnitude-based approaches elsewhere that are contested
tentsr_applicability: Stage 2 CV% for EMG amplitude; report systematic change in mean separately

citation: Bland JM, Altman DG. Measuring agreement in method comparison studies. Stat Methods Med Res 1999;8(2):135-160
results_effects_uncertainty: LoA with CIs (SE of LoA approx sqrt(3/n)*s); regression-based LoA for non-constant bias/SD; repeated-measures handled in separate Bland & Altman paper
limitations_coi: Repeated-measures section not verified
tentsr_applicability: Stage 2/3 agreement analysis and Example 1 sample-size arithmetic
access: SECONDARY (search snippets incl. Chatfield Stata Journal)

citation: Lu MJ, Zhong WH, Liu YX, Miao HZ, Li YC, Ji MH. Sample size for assessing agreement between two methods of measurement by Bland-Altman method. Int J Biostat 2016;12(2)
results_effects_uncertainty: Power-based n so that CI of LoA lies within a predefined clinical margin, given alpha, beta, mean and SD of differences; implemented in MedCalc and R blandPower
limitations_coi: Full text paywalled; formula not reproduced here
tentsr_applicability: Stage 3 sample size once pilot SD of differences is known

citation: Bonett DG. Sample size requirements for estimating intraclass correlations with desired precision. Stat Med 2002;21:1331-1335
results_effects_uncertainty: Approximate n for target ICC CI width; worked example k=4, ICC 0.85, width 0.2 gives n=19.2 (reproduced numerically by A5)
limitations_coi: Approximation; targets expected width without assurance
tentsr_applicability: Stage 2 Example 2

citation: Zou GY. Sample size formulas for estimating intraclass correlation coefficients with precision and assurance. Stat Med 2012;31(29):3972-3981
doi_or_link: 10.1002/sim.5466 (DOI not seen in search results - UNVERIFIED)
results_effects_uncertainty: Adds assurance probability to precision-based ICC sample size; implemented in R ICC.Sample.Size
limitations_coi: DOI not confirmed in this session
tentsr_applicability: Stage 2: n with assurance > Bonett n

citation: Hermens HJ, Freriks B, Disselhorst-Klug C, Rau G. Development of recommendations for SEMG sensors and sensor placement procedures. J Electromyogr Kinesiol 2000;10(5):361-374
results_effects_uncertainty: Placement procedures and sensor recommendations (SENIAM 8)
limitations_coi: Consensus, not empirical validation; gel electrodes
tentsr_applicability: Reference electrode placement in Stage 3; TENSR 25.4 mm IED vs SENIAM recommendations is A3's question

citation: Farina D, Merletti R. Comparison of algorithms for estimation of EMG variables during voluntary isometric contractions. J Electromyogr Kinesiol 2000;10(5):337-349
design: methods comparison on simulated and experimental signals
results_effects_uncertainty: Established practice of testing spectral estimators on simulated signals with known MDF; estimator variance depends on epoch length (SECONDARY via Corvini 2022)
limitations_coi: Isometric only; details not read
tentsr_applicability: Stage 1 S1.3 design: synthetic EMG with known MDF

citation: Lynn SK, et al. Validity and reliability of surface electromyography measurements from a wearable athlete performance system. J Sports Sci Med 2018;17:205-215
exercise_muscle_contraction: quadriceps-type knee extension repetitions (details not read)
hardware_processing: Athos garment textile sEMG vs research-grade electrodes placed just distal on same muscle
results_effects_uncertainty: No significant effect of system on repetition amplitude metrics; normalised amplitude variability 12% (Athos) vs 10.7% (research)
limitations_coi: n=12; concluded validity from non-significance (not equivalence); manufacturer involvement not checked
tentsr_applicability: Template for concurrent adjacent placement in Stage 3; shows what not to infer

citation: Saeb S, Lonini L, Jayaraman A, Mohr DC, Kording KP. The need to approximate the use-case in clinical machine learning. GigaScience 2017;6(5):gix019
results_effects_uncertainty: Record-wise CV often massively overestimates accuracy vs subject-wise
limitations_coi: Little and Varoquaux argue subject-wise CV is not always sufficient (gix020)
tentsr_applicability: Stage 4 LOSO requirement and leakage checklist

citation: Van Calster B, McLernon DJ, van Smeden M, Wynants L, Steyerberg EW. Calibration: the Achilles heel of predictive analytics. BMC Med 2019;17:230
results_effects_uncertainty: Calibration should be assessed in validation; poorly calibrated model can be less useful than a better-calibrated lower-AUC one
limitations_coi: Clinical risk-model framing
tentsr_applicability: Stage 4 calibration plots and slope for RIR predictions

citation: Riley RD, Ensor J, Snell KIE, et al. Calculating the sample size required for developing a clinical prediction model. BMJ 2020;368:m441
results_effects_uncertainty: Replaces rules of thumb with criteria incl. precise intercept and limited overfitting; pmsampsize package
limitations_coi: Clinical framing; continuous-outcome criteria apply to RIR
tentsr_applicability: Stage 4 model development n

citation: Riley RD, Snell KIE, Archer L, et al. Evaluation of clinical prediction models (part 3): calculating the sample size required for an external validation study. BMJ 2024;384:e074821
results_effects_uncertainty: n=100 too small for stable calibration; tailored calculations via pmvalsampsize; validation data must be representative
limitations_coi: Author list beyond Riley from snippets only
tentsr_applicability: Stage 4 frozen-model external validation

citation: Halperin I, Malleron T, Har-Nir I, Androulakis-Korakakis P, Wolf M, Fisher J, Steele J. Accuracy in predicting repetitions to task failure in resistance exercise: a scoping review and exploratory meta-analysis. Sports Med 2022;52(2):377-390
results_effects_uncertainty: Mean underprediction 0.95 reps; I2 = 97.9%; better closer to failure, heavier loads, later sets; training status little effect
limitations_coi: Very high heterogeneity; exploratory
tentsr_applicability: Self-reported RIR is not ground truth; benchmark TENSR must beat

citation: Steele J, Fisher J, Giessing J, Gentil P. Clarity in reporting terminology and definitions of set end points in resistance training. Muscle Nerve 2017;56(3):368-374
results_effects_uncertainty: Proposes clearer definitions of set end points incl. momentary failure
limitations_coi: Definitions themselves not read
tentsr_applicability: Failure labelling protocol in Stage 4

citation: Steele J, Endres A, Fisher J, Gentil P, Giessing J. Ability to predict repetitions to momentary failure is not perfectly accurate, though improves with resistance training experience. PeerJ 2017;5:e4105
results_effects_uncertainty: Participants underpredicted reps to failure; RIR should be used cautiously
limitations_coi: Details not read
tentsr_applicability: Self-report RIR baseline

citation: Sanchez-Medina L, Gonzalez-Badillo JJ. Velocity loss as an indicator of neuromuscular fatigue during resistance training. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2011;43(9):1725-1734
exercise_muscle_contraction: bench press and squat, various set configurations
results_effects_uncertainty: Velocity loss correlated with lactate r=0.93-0.97 and CMJ loss r~0.92 (SECONDARY)
limitations_coi: Correlations are group-level, not individual accuracy
tentsr_applicability: Velocity loss as Stage 4 reference target, not available to TENSR users

citation: Jukic I, et al. Modeling the repetitions-in-reserve-velocity relationship: a valid method for resistance training monitoring and prescription, and fatigue management. Physiol Rep 2024
comparator_reference: actual RIR from sets to failure
results_effects_uncertainty: Individual RIR-velocity relationships fitted better than general; only individual relationships from session 1 gave mean error <2 reps in session 2
limitations_coi: Author list, n not verified (search budget)
tentsr_applicability: Precedent for per-user calibration and new-session testing in Stage 4

citation: Jukic I, et al. Prediction of percentage of completed repetitions to failure using velocity loss. Eur J Appl Physiol 2023
results_effects_uncertainty: Predictive ability of general and individual VL-%reps relationships poor; advised against use for free-weight squat
limitations_coi: Title/authors from snippet only
tentsr_applicability: Warns that a fatigue index within a set may predict reps-left poorly

citation: Garcia-Ramos A, et al. Prediction of the maximum number of repetitions and repetitions in reserve from barbell velocity. Int J Sports Physiol Perform 2018
results_effects_uncertainty: General equation for velocity at given RIR failed to give acceptable between-subject variability; individualised relationships needed
limitations_coi: Journal and details from snippet only - UNVERIFIED
tentsr_applicability: Population vs individual calibration in Stage 4

citation: Lorenzetti S, et al. Validity and reliability of simple measurement device to assess the velocity of the barbell during squats. BMC Res Notes 2017;10:707
results_effects_uncertainty: LPTs valid for mean velocity in squats (r 0.932-0.990); accelerometer less accurate
limitations_coi: n=9; article number 707 UNVERIFIED
tentsr_applicability: Supports LPT as Stage 3/4 velocity reference for squat; less so deadlift (Dorrell, SECONDARY)

citation: Weakley J, et al. Visual feedback attenuates mean concentric barbell velocity loss and improves motivation, competitiveness, and perceived workload in male adolescent athletes. J Strength Cond Res 2019;33(9)
results_effects_uncertainty: Mean velocity 0.70 vs 0.65 m/s; larger difference late in set; higher motivation
limitations_coi: Magnitude-based inference; adolescents; acute only
tentsr_applicability: Precedent for Stage 5 acute crossover

citation: Weakley J, Till K, Sampson J, Banyard H, Leduc C, Wilson K, Roe G, Jones B. The effects of augmented feedback on sprint, jump, and strength adaptations in rugby union players after a 4-week training program. Int J Sports Physiol Perform 2019;14(9):1205-1211
results_effects_uncertainty: CMJ relative peak power, 10/20 m sprint and 3RM squat 'possibly to likely' greater with feedback
limitations_coi: Small n, short, magnitude-based inference
tentsr_applicability: Only longitudinal feedback precedent; weak support for Stage 5 benefit

citation: Weakley J, et al. Show me, tell me, encourage me: the effect of different forms of feedback on resistance training performance. J Strength Cond Res 2020;34(11):3157-3163
hardware_processing: verbal kinematic, visual kinematic, verbal encouragement
results_effects_uncertainty: All forms improved velocity vs control; differences between forms trivial; encouragement may help low-conscientiousness individuals
limitations_coi: n=12; acute
tentsr_applicability: Stage 5 control arms need attention/encouragement matching

citation: Weakley J, et al. The effect of feedback on resistance training performance and adaptations: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Sports Med 2023;53(9):1789-1803
results_effects_uncertainty: Acute velocity +~8.4% (g~0.63); visual g 1.11 vs verbal g 0.47 vs no feedback
limitations_coi: Pooled participant n and certainty not retrieved
tentsr_applicability: Supports acute effect of feedback; long-term evidence thin

citation: Jimenez-Alonso A, Garcia-Ramos A, Cepero M, Miras-Moreno S, Rojas FJ, Perez-Castilla A. Effect of augmented feedback on velocity performance during strength-oriented and power-oriented resistance training sessions. J Strength Cond Res 2022;36(6):1511-1517
status: published (one record lists 2020 - online-first year likely)
results_effects_uncertainty: Result UNVERIFIED; Weakley2023 reports authors suggested verbal velocity feedback may matter more in strength-oriented than ballistic training (SECONDARY)
limitations_coi: Not read
tentsr_applicability: Named in brief; cannot be used as support until abstract read

citation: Orange ST, Hritz A, Pearson L, et al. Comparison of the effects of velocity-based vs traditional resistance training methods on adaptations in strength, power, and sprint speed: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and quality of evidence appraisal. J Sports Sci 2022;40(11):1220-1234
design: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
results_effects_uncertainty: Strength SMD 0.06 (95% CI -0.51 to 0.63); power 0.11 (-0.28 to 0.49); sprint -0.10 (-0.72 to 0.53); low to very low certainty
limitations_coi: Few small trials; imprecise, not equivalence
tentsr_applicability: No established long-term benefit of objective-feedback training; frames Stage 5 effect size

citation: NHMRC, ARC, Universities Australia. National Statement on Ethical Conduct in Human Research 2023
status: in effect from 1 Jan 2024; NHMRC pages reference a 2025 edition with changed/delayed effective date - check at application
results_effects_uncertainty: Two-category risk model (lower/higher); risk of harm beyond discomfort = higher risk requiring HREC review
limitations_coi: Edition in force on application date must be checked
tentsr_applicability: Stages 2-5 likely higher-risk HREC review

citation: Therapeutic Goods Administration. Understanding the general health or wellness software exclusion (Excluded Goods Determination item 14B, from 25 Feb 2021)
results_effects_uncertainty: Wellness monitoring via non-invasive measurement excluded; every function must qualify; e.g. fitness wearable excluded, heart-rate warning for irregularity not excluded
limitations_coi: Applies to software (incl. with non-invasive hardware); legal advice needed for hardware edge cases
tentsr_applicability: Keep study and product language to training/performance; no injury/rehab/diagnosis
